why: The verifier brief is fine on item 1. Check 1's PASS and FAIL conditions only ask that the call does not throw and returns `{}`. The stderr message naming the file is listed under "Advisory (does not affect PASS/FAIL)". The builder brief breaks item 2. Step 2 tells the builder that "in the catch, also write one line to stderr ... that names `path` and includes the parse error's message". So on a parse error the builder must do more than return {}: it must also log a warning. That is the same extra behaviour must_not item 1 forbids in a verifier condition. Step 4 also has the builder rewrite README.md to describe "a warning naming the file". Acceptance line 1 asks only for catching the error and returning {}, so the builder brief goes past it. The criterion fails.
